subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should Mattermost native slash command registration fail closed for every non-HTTPS callback URL, including explicit HTTP URLs, or should existing HTTP deployments get a staged or opt-in policy first?
rationale: The patch protects a token-bearing callback boundary but intentionally breaks existing HTTP callback deployments, so automation cannot choose the security and upgrade tradeoff for maintainers.

options.title: Accept HTTPS-only fail closed
options.body: Land this policy after the contributor adds real Mattermost proof and the branch is made mergeable.

options.title: Stage compatibility
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved staged or opt-in strict-mode path if preserving existing HTTP deployments is more important for this release.

options.title: Replace the branch
options.body: Close or supersede this PR only after a narrower maintainer-owned replacement keeps the same transport security goal.

recommendation.title: Accept HTTPS-only fail closed
recommendation.body: Land this policy after the contributor adds real Mattermost proof and the branch is made mergeable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows steipete split the monitor helper and hardened adjacent slash token validation, making this the best available routing signal for the security-boundary decision.
